value.body: A degree in news, media and communication. You study reporting and editing, media law and ethics, advertising and public relations, and radio, TV and digital production, usually with hands-on projects and an internship. Some universities offer the same subject as a BA (Journalism & Mass Communication).

items.label: Course length
items.note: 4-year honours option at some universities under NEP 2020

items.label: Students enrolled
items.note: All modes; B.J. and BA (JMC) programmes are counted separately

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 in any stream. Admission is through CUET-UG at many central and state universities, a university's own entrance test, or Class 12 merit.

value.title: At a glance
items: Newsrooms and agencies often look closely at published work and internships, not only marks.
Work spans news, digital content, advertising, PR and corporate communication.
A master's or PG diploma (for example at IIMC, via CUET-PG) is one route to specialise.
